title: Tether Link Utility: Share Your Phone's Mobile Data via SOCKS5
ogTitle: Tether Link Utility: Share Your Phone's Mobile Data via SOCKS5
description: Share your Android phone's mobile data with your laptop, tablet or another phone through a local SOCKS5 proxy. No root, no account, no remote server.

howTo.name: How to share your phone's mobile data over Wi-Fi with Tether Link Utility

steps.name: Tap START SHARING
steps.text: The Wi-Fi hotspot turns on automatically and the app starts a local SOCKS5 proxy on the phone. The first time, tap Allow, then OK in the phone's Connection request window.

steps.name: Pick the other device
steps.text: Tap the device that will use the phone's internet: Android, Windows, iPhone, Mac, Linux or Other (TV, game console). For a Windows PC or a Mac, the app starts with the one file to download: it installs and runs sing-box for you, so every app works. For a phone, it asks whether the app is installed and shows how to install it, even without internet.

steps.name: Connect your device
steps.text: Android: on the other phone, tap Use another phone's internet, then Scan QR code. Windows PC or Mac: join the Wi-Fi shown (it may say "No internet"; that's normal), open the setup file (Windows) or the script (Mac) and type the two values. iPhone or Linux: enter the two values in Potatso or Firefox. The app's screen waits by itself until the device connects.

steps.name: Start browsing
steps.text: Traffic routes through your mobile data. No remote server, everything stays on your device.

items.q: How does Tether Link Utility work?
items.a: It runs a local SOCKS5 proxy on your Android phone, using Android's VpnService API, and shares it over the phone's Wi-Fi hotspot (no USB cable involved). Your other devices send their traffic to that proxy, and the phone forwards it over its mobile data connection. There's no remote server in between.
No, it works entirely without root privileges.

items.q: Does it use a remote server?
items.a: No. Proxied traffic goes from your devices to your phone and out over your mobile data; it is not routed through, logged, or stored on any server of ours. The free version shows Google AdMob ads, and the app uses Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics, which collect device identifiers and usage and crash data, as described in our privacy policy.

items.q: Can I connect a Windows or Mac laptop?
items.a: Yes. On Windows, download the setup file; on a Mac, the script. Each one installs and runs sing-box for you, so every app on the computer, DNS included, uses the phone's internet. Then type the IP and port shown in the app. Options that cover fewer apps (Firefox, FoxyProxy, the Mac's proxy setting) also exist. Written steps. ▶︎ Watch the Windows video (1:21) ▶︎ Watch the Mac video (1:19)

items.q: Does a SOCKS5 proxy setting protect all my traffic?
items.a: Not entirely. A browser or system SOCKS5 setting only reroutes traffic from apps that check it; DNS lookups and other background traffic can still go over the plain hotspot connection. For full coverage, use the Windows setup file or the Mac script: they run sing-box in TUN mode and send the whole computer's traffic, DNS included, through the phone. ▶︎ Watch the Windows video (1:21) ▶︎ Watch the Mac video (1:19)

iOS has no native SOCKS5 setting, but apps like Potatso or Shadowrocket can connect to the proxy the same way, for that app's own traffic only, not the whole device. A verified full-device option isn't currently available on iOS. A native iOS app is in development and coming soon.

items.q: How many devices can connect at once?
items.a: The free tier connects 1 device at a time; Pro raises that to 5. Pro starts from $3.99/month. The exact price, including local currency and yearly plan, is shown in Google Play.
Yes, it shares whatever active mobile data connection your phone currently has, regardless of network generation.

items.q: Does it use my mobile data plan?
items.a: Yes. Data used by connected devices counts toward your plan. Check your carrier's terms for tethering.

Yes, the free version is free to use: 1 device at a time, with ads. Pro removes ads and allows up to 5 devices at once. The app itself doesn't currently add a speed limit; actual speed depends on your carrier, plan and signal.

items.q: Can other devices join my own hotspot by scanning the QR code?
items.a: Yes. If you turn on your phone's system hotspot yourself (Mobile Hotspot on Android, Personal Hotspot on iPhone), save its network name and password once with Add hotspot Wi-Fi details in the app. They are stored only on your device, the app doesn't change your hotspot settings, and the details are added to the QR code so other devices join the network automatically by scanning. On iPhone, the password is shown in Settings > Personal Hotspot. When the Android app starts its own hotspot automatically, this step isn't needed.
